title: A recording can be made small enough to send
goal: A screen recording is the file most likely to be too big to send, and MP4 is the one format in the Export sheet with nothing you can do about it. The sheet can already tell you a recording will weigh 200 MB; it offers you High, Standard and Small for a GIF and nothing at all for an MP4. Give MP4 the same three choices, so a clip you want to put in a chat can be made to fit.
notes:
This is NOT a new control. VideoExportQuality already exists in Sources/PhotonzCore/Recording.swift with high, standard and small, each carrying a targetFPS and a maxDimension, and RecordingExportDialog already draws the Quality row as a segmented picker. The row is hidden for MP4 by RecordingExport.offersQuality, which the file itself comments as "MP4 has none yet". So this is finishing the row that shipped on 2026-09-19, not adding a new one, and it does not need a decision card.

What actually has to change: VideoExporter.exportMP4 is pinned to AVAssetExportPresetHighestQuality, so there is nothing behind the choice yet. Map the three presets onto real encode settings and keep the fast path: an untouched recording exported at the top choice is still a verbatim file copy and must stay one.

The estimate. RecordingExport.sizeLine already works an MP4 estimate out from what the recording itself costs per second and per pixel, and on the eight second sample it said "about 16 KB" against 16,531 bytes landing. Re-check it per preset rather than trusting the one that exists.

Comes from the 2026-09-19-recording-export-sheet audit rough list, word for word: "There is still no way to make an MP4 smaller. The sheet can now tell you a recording will weigh 200 MB and offers you nothing to do about it." The user who asked for the whole trim-and-send flow ended their sentence with "send in teams", which is the case this serves.
acceptance: The Quality row appears for MP4 as well as GIF and HEIC, with the same three choices
Each choice says what it means in the line under it, the way the animated formats already do: the frame rate and the pixel size the file will come out at
The weight estimate under it moves when you change the choice, and the estimate is checked against a file actually written for each of the three
An untouched recording exported at the top choice still takes the verbatim copy fast path, so nothing gets slower or re-encoded for no reason
The choice is remembered between exports, like the format already is
Ships behind next-recording-export-sheet; the try path is: open a recording from History, press Shift Command S, pick MP4, and the Quality row is there with the weight moving as you change it
audit written under queue/audits/, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar and written into this task log if it does not

log.note: done as part of getting-a-recording-out-is-quick-and-the-file-is, which landed in 2a900df4. Everything this task asked for is in: the Quality row appears for MP4 with the same three choices, each says the frame rate and pixel size it will land at on the line under it, the weight moves when you change it and was checked against files actually written at each of the three (147/147 exact for the copy, 147/134 Standard, 96/108 Small), an untouched recording at the top choice still takes the verbatim copy fast path, and the choice is remembered per format so picking Small for a GIF does not quietly shrink the next video. The one place it went further: VideoExportQuality.recipe gives MP4 its own meaning for the three words rather than reusing the animated 24/15/10 fps and 1280/800/480 caps, because High on a video has to mean the recording as it is or the fast path goes. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-21-recording-export-size.json.
